title: Hands Off the Glovebox: An Electrochemical System for Semiautonomous Decontamination at Los Alamos
summary: The radiological glovebox is among the most recognizable pieces of contaminated infrastructure in the nuclear enterprise, and among the most difficult for disposition. Every glovebox used in plutonium operations eventually reaches the end of its service life. It can be dispositioned in its contaminated state, but at considerable cost: disposal as transuranic (TRU) waste is orders of magnitude more expensive than disposal as low-level waste, and it consumes limited capacity at the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant in Carlsbad, N.M., the nation’s only deep geologic repository for defense TRU waste. This economic reality makes decontamination to LLW limits the strongly preferred disposition path. Today, that work is typically performed by an operator reaching through glove ports to repeatedly spray and wipe interior surfaces until surveys confirm acceptable contamination levels. The process is slow, physically demanding, and dose-intensive, and the wipes, rags, and spent reagents it consumes become radioactive waste themselves.

title: NRC hosts FERC for joint meeting on nuclear generation, grid reliability
summary: Twenty years ago, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission held their first joint meeting, spurred by the 2003 Northeast blackout during which, among other things, nine U.S. nuclear reactors tripped off line.

title: Radiant Industries chosen for naval station deployment
summary: On Wednesday, the Department of the Navy announced that it has selected Radiant Industries to design, build, and deliver a “prototype microreactor power plant” featuring the company’s Kaleidos design for the Naval Weapons Station Crane in Indiana.

title: Nano Nuclear Signs Engineering Agreement With Argentina’s IMPSA For Kronos Microreactor
summary: US advanced reactor developer Nano Nuclear Energy has signed a three-year engineering services agreement with the US subsidiary of Argentina’s IMPSA to assess the design and manufacture of key components for its Kronos microreactor, a statement said. According to the statement, the initial work would be an approximately six-month design review and manufacturing feasibility study, with the reactor pressure vessel a principal component under assessment.
